dropped.finding: The new authorship-gate scope exemption drops EVERY event whose type is not in reducer.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES, but that set excludes state-bearing PRECONDITIONS (and bridge SYNC) events — not just pure observability sidecars. PRECONDITIONS carries gate_verdicts/manifest_depth that the reducer folds into ticket state, so under enforcement a forged/unsigned PRECONDITIONS event is silently removed from authorship verification.
scenarios: identity.require_authenticated is on; an attacker (or a mis-provisioned seam with no signing key) writes an unsigned or forged PRECONDITIONS event carrying favorable gate_verdicts; the gate skips it (returns []) instead of classifying it unsigned/bad-signature, so the run still exits 0
A SYNC bridge event with a forged author_sig is likewise never classified by the gate under enforcement
dropped.suggested_fix: Do not key the exemption on KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES alone. Instead skip only an explicit allowlist of pure observability sidecars (e.g. COMPLETION_VERDICT/REVIEW_RESULT/TICKET_DIGEST/ENQUEUE_ENRICH/CLAIM_ENRICH/DONE_ENRICH), and keep PRECONDITIONS and SYNC in scope so their author_sig is still verified under enforcement.
